verses.zh: 耶和华在西奈山对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses at Mount Sinai:

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：你们到了我所赐你们那地的时候，地就要向耶和华守安息。
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them, ‘When you enter the land that I am giving you, the land must observe a Sabbath[NOTE:1] to the Lord.
notes: Heb “the land shall rest a Sabbath.”

verses.zh: 六年要耕种田地，也要修理葡萄园，收藏地的出产。
verses.en: Six years you may sow your field, and six years you may prune your vineyard and gather the produce,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “its produce,” but the feminine pronoun “its” probably refers to the “land” (a feminine noun in Hebrew; cf. v. 2), not the “field” or the “vineyard,” both of which are normally masculine nouns (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 170).

verses.zh: 第七年，地要守圣安息，就是向耶和华守的安息，不可耕种田地，也不可修理葡萄园。
verses.en: but in the seventh year the land must have a Sabbath of complete rest[NOTE:1]—a Sabbath to the Lord. You must not sow your field or[NOTE:2] prune your vineyard.
notes: Heb “and in the seventh year a Sabbath of complete rest shall be to the land.” The expression “a Sabbath of complete rest” is superlative, emphasizing the full and all inclusive rest of the seventh year of the sabbatical cycle. Cf. ASV “a sabbath of solemn rest”; NAB “a complete rest.”
Heb “and.” Here the Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) has an alternative sense (“or”).

verses.zh: 遗落自长的庄稼不可收割；没有修理的葡萄树也不可摘取葡萄。这年，地要守圣安息。
verses.en: You must not gather in the aftergrowth of your harvest, and you must not pick the grapes of your unpruned vines;[NOTE:1] the land must have a year of complete rest.
notes: Heb “consecrated, devoted, forbidden” (נָזִיר, nazir). The same term is used for the “consecration” of the “Nazirite” (and his hair, Num 6:2, 18, etc.), a designation which, in turn, derives from the very same root.

verses.zh: 地在安息年所出的，要给你和你的仆人、婢女、雇工人，并寄居的外人当食物。
verses.en: You may have the Sabbath produce[NOTE:1] of the land to eat—you, your male servant, your female servant, your hired worker, the resident foreigner who stays with you,[NOTE:2]
notes: The word “produce” is not in the Hebrew text but is implied; cf. NASB “the sabbath products.”
A “resident who stays” would be a foreign person who was probably residing as another kind of laborer in the household of a landowner (B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 170-71). See v. 35 below.

verses.zh: 这年的土产也要给你的牲畜和你地上的走兽当食物。」
verses.en: your cattle, and the wild animals that are in your land—all its produce will be for you[NOTE:1] to eat.
notes: The words “for you” are implied.

verses.zh: 「你要计算七个安息年，就是七七年。这便为你成了七个安息年，共是四十九年。
verses.en: “‘You must count off[NOTE:1] seven weeks of years, seven times seven years,[NOTE:2] and the days of the seven weeks of years will amount to 49 years.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And you shall count off for yourself.”
Heb “seven years seven times.”
Heb “and they shall be for you, the days of the seven Sabbaths of years, forty-nine years.”

verses.zh: 当年七月初十日，你要大发角声；这日就是赎罪日，要在遍地发出角声。
verses.en: You must sound loud horn blasts[NOTE:1]—in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, on the Day of Atonement—you must sound the horn in your entire land.
notes: On the “loud horn blasts” see the note on Lev 23:24, but unlike the language there, the Hebrew term for “horn” (שׁוֹפָר, shofar) actually appears here in this verse (twice).

verses.zh: 第五十年，你们要当作圣年，在遍地给一切的居民宣告自由。这年必为你们的禧年，各人要归自己的产业，各归本家。
verses.en: So you must consecrate the fiftieth year,[NOTE:1] and you must proclaim a release[NOTE:2] in the land for all its inhabitants. That year will be your Jubilee;[NOTE:3] each one of you must return[NOTE:4] to his property, and each one of you must return to his clan.
notes: Heb “the year of the fifty years,” or perhaps “the year, fifty years” (GKC 435 §134.o, note 2).

Cf. KJV, ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV “liberty”; TEV, CEV “freedom.” The characteristics of this “release” are detailed in the following verses. For substantial summaries and bibliography on the biblical and ancient Near Eastern material regarding such a “release” see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 427-34, and B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 270-74.

Heb “A jubilee that shall be to you.” Although there has been some significant debate about the original meaning of the Hebrew word translated “jubilee” (יוֹבֵל, yovel; see the summary in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 434), the term most likely means “ram” and can refer also to a “ram’s horn.” The fiftieth year would, therefore, be called the “jubilee” because of the associated sounding of the “ram’s horn” (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 172, and the literature cited there).
Heb “you [plural] shall return, a man.”

verses.zh: 第五十年要作为你们的禧年。这年不可耕种；地中自长的，不可收割；没有修理的葡萄树也不可摘取葡萄。
verses.en: That fiftieth year will be your Jubilee; you must not sow the land, harvest its aftergrowth, or pick the grapes of its unpruned vines.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you shall not sow and you shall not…and you shall not….”sn See v. 5 above and the notes there.

verses.zh: 因为这是禧年，你们要当作圣年，吃地中自出的土产。
verses.en: Because that year is a Jubilee, it will be holy to you—you may eat its produce[NOTE:1] from the field.
notes: That is, the produce of the land (fem.; cf. v. 7 above).

verses.zh: 「这禧年，你们各人要归自己的地业。
verses.en: “‘In this Year of Jubilee you must each return[NOTE:1] to your property.
notes: Heb “you [plural] shall return, a man.”

verses.zh: 你若卖甚么给邻舍，或是从邻舍的手中买甚么，彼此不可亏负。
verses.en: If you make a sale[NOTE:1] to your fellow citizen[NOTE:2] or buy[NOTE:3] from your fellow citizen, no one is to wrong his brother.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “sell a sale.”
Or “to one of your countrymen” NIV84; NIV11 “to any of your own people”; NASB “to your friend.”
The Hebrew infinitive absolute קָנֹה (qanoh, “buying”) substitutes for the finite verb here in sequence with the previous finite verb “sell” at the beginning of the verse (see GKC 345 §113.z).
Heb “do not oppress a man his brother.” Here “brother” does not refer only to a sibling, but to a fellow Israelite.

verses.zh: 你要按禧年以后的年数向邻舍买；他也要按年数的收成卖给你。
verses.en: You may buy it from your fellow citizen according to the number of years since[NOTE:1] the last Jubilee; he may sell it to you according to the years of produce that are left.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the number of years after.”

The purchaser is actually buying only the crops that the land will produce until the next Jubilee, since the land will revert to the original owner at that time. The purchaser, therefore, is not actually buying the land itself. tn The words “that are left” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied.

verses.zh: 年岁若多，要照数加添价值；年岁若少，要照数减去价值，因为他照收成的数目卖给你。
verses.en: The more years there are,[NOTE:1] the more you may make its purchase price, and the fewer years there are,[NOTE:2] the less you must make its purchase price, because he is only selling to you a number of years of[NOTE:3] produce.
notes: Heb “To the mouth of the many years.”
Heb “to the mouth of the few years.”
Heb “a number of produce”; the words “years of” are implied. As an alternative this could be translated “a number of harvests” (cf. NRSV, NLT).

verses.zh: 你们彼此不可亏负，只要敬畏你们的　神，因为我是耶和华―你们的　神。」
verses.en: No one is to oppress his fellow citizen,[NOTE:1] but you must fear your God, because I am the Lord your God.
notes: Heb “And you shall not oppress a man his fellow citizen.”

verses.zh: 「我的律例，你们要遵行，我的典章，你们要谨守，就可以在那地上安然居住。
verses.en: You must obey my statutes and my regulations; you must be sure to keep them[NOTE:1] so that you may live securely in the land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And you shall keep and do them.” This appears to be a kind of verbal hendiadys, where the first verb is a modifier of the action of the second verb (see GKC 386 §120.d, although שָׁמַר [shamar, “to keep”] is not cited there; cf. Lev 20:8, etc.).
Heb “and you shall dwell on the land to security.”

verses.zh: 地必出土产，你们就要吃饱，在那地上安然居住。
verses.en: “‘The land will give its fruit, and you may eat until you are satisfied,[NOTE:1] and you may live securely in the land.
notes: Heb “eat to satisfaction”; KJV, ASV “ye shall eat your fill.”

verses.zh: 你们若说：『这第七年我们不耕种，也不收藏土产，吃甚么呢？』
verses.en: If you say, “What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow and gather our produce?”

verses.zh: 我必在第六年将我所命的福赐给你们，地便生三年的土产。
verses.en: I will command my blessing for you in the sixth year so that it may yield[NOTE:1] the produce[NOTE:2] for three years,
notes: Heb “and it [i.e., the land] shall make the produce.” The Hebrew term וְעָשָׂת (veʿasat, “and it shall make”) is probably an older third feminine singular form of the verb (GKC 210 §75.m). Smr has the normal form.
Smr and LXX have “its produce” (cf. 25:3, 7, etc.) rather than “the produce.”

verses.zh: 第八年，你们要耕种，也要吃陈粮，等到第九年出产收来的时候，你们还吃陈粮。」
verses.en: and you may sow the eighth year and eat from that sixth year’s produce[NOTE:1]—old produce. Until you bring in the ninth year’s produce,[NOTE:2] you may eat old produce.
notes: Heb “the produce,” referring to “the produce” of the sixth year of v. 21. The words “sixth year” are supplied for clarity.
Heb “until the ninth year, until bringing [in] its produce.”

verses.zh: 「地不可永卖，因为地是我的；你们在我面前是客旅，是寄居的。
verses.en: The land must not be sold without reclaim[NOTE:1] because the land belongs to me, for you are foreign residents, temporary settlers, with me.[NOTE:2]
notes: The term rendered “without reclaim” means that the land has been bought for the full price and is, therefore, not subject to reclaim under any circumstances. This was not to be done with land in ancient Israel (contrast the final full sale of houses in v. 30; see the evidence cited in B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 174).

Abraham refers to himself by these terms in Gen 23:4. Ps 39:12 and 1 Chr 29:15 take up this language from Lev 25:23.tn The Hebrew terms ger (גֵּר; “resident foreigner”) and toshav (תּוֹשָׁב; “resident/dweller”) have similar meaning. The toshav was less integrated into Israelite society, had less rights, and had not fully committed to the religion of Israel. But in this context the terms are used simply to emphasize that Israel would be a guest on God’s land. They were attached to the Lord’s household. They did not own the land.

verses.zh: 在你们所得为业的全地，也要准人将地赎回。
verses.en: In all your landed property[NOTE:1] you must provide for the right of redemption of the land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And in all the land of your property.”
Heb “right of redemption you shall give to the land”; NAB “you must permit the land to be redeemed.”

verses.zh: 你的弟兄（弟兄是指本国人说；下同）若渐渐穷乏，卖了几分地业，他至近的亲属就要来把弟兄所卖的赎回。
verses.en: “‘If your brother becomes impoverished and sells some of his property, his near redeemer is to come to you and redeem what his brother sold.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the sale of his brother.”

verses.zh: 若没有能给他赎回的，他自己渐渐富足，能够赎回，
verses.en: If a man has no redeemer, but he prospers[NOTE:1] and gains enough for its redemption,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and his hand reaches.”
Heb “and he finds as sufficiency of its redemption.”

verses.zh: 就要算出卖地的年数，把余剩年数的价值还那买主，自己便归回自己的地业。
verses.en: he is to calculate the value of the years it was sold,[NOTE:1] refund the balance[NOTE:2] to the man to whom he had sold it, and return to his property.
notes: Heb “and he shall calculate its years of sale.”
Heb “and return the excess.”

verses.zh: 倘若不能为自己得回所卖的，仍要存在买主的手里直到禧年；到了禧年，地业要出买主的手，自己便归回自己的地业。
verses.en: If he has not prospered enough to refund[NOTE:1] a balance to him, then what he sold[NOTE:2] will belong to[NOTE:3] the one who bought it until the Jubilee year, but it must revert[NOTE:4] in the Jubilee and the original owner[NOTE:5] may return to his property.
notes: Heb “And if his hand has not found sufficiency of returning.” Although some versions take this to mean that he has not made enough to regain the land (e.g., NASB, NRSV; see also B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 176), the combination of terms in Hebrew corresponds to the portion of v. 27 that refers specifically to refunding the money (cf. v. 27; see NIV and G. J. Wenham, Leviticus [NICOT], 315).
Heb “his sale.”
Heb “will be in the hand of.” This refers to the temporary control of the one who purchased its produce until the next Year of Jubilee, at which time it would revert to the original owner.
Heb “it shall go out” (so KJV, ASV; see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 176).
Heb “he”; the referent (the original owner of the land) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 「人若卖城内的住宅，卖了以后，一年之内可以赎回；在一整年，必有赎回的权柄。
verses.en: “‘If a man sells a residential house in a walled city,[NOTE:1] its right of redemption must extend[NOTE:2] until one full year from its sale;[NOTE:3] its right of redemption must extend to a full calendar year.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “a house of a residence of a walled city.”
Heb “shall be.”
Heb “of its sale.”
Heb “days its right of redemption shall be” (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 176).

verses.zh: 若在一整年之内不赎回，这城内的房屋就定准永归买主，世世代代为业；在禧年也不得出买主的手。
verses.en: If it is not redeemed before the full calendar year is ended,[NOTE:1] the house in the walled city[NOTE:2] will belong without reclaim[NOTE:3] to the one who bought it throughout his generations; it will not revert in the Jubilee.
notes: Heb “until fulfilling to it a complete year.’
Heb “the house which [is] in the city which to it [is] a wall.” The Kethib has לֹא (loʾ, “no, not”) rather than לוֹ (lo, “to it”) which is the Qere.
See the note on v. 23 above.

verses.zh: 但房屋在无城墙的村庄里，要看如乡下的田地一样，可以赎回；到了禧年，都要出买主的手。
verses.en: The houses of villages, however,[NOTE:1] which have no wall surrounding them[NOTE:2] must be considered as the field[NOTE:3] of the land; they will have the right of redemption and must revert in the Jubilee.
notes: Heb “And the houses of the villages.”
Heb “which there is not to them a wall.”
Heb “on the field.”

verses.zh: 然而利未人所得为业的城邑，其中的房屋，利未人可以随时赎回。
verses.en: As for[NOTE:1] the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities which they possess,[NOTE:2] the Levites must have a perpetual right of redemption.
notes: Heb “And.”
Heb “the houses of the cities of their property.”

verses.zh: 若是一个利未人不将所卖的房屋赎回，是在所得为业的城内，到了禧年就要出买主的手，因为利未人城邑的房屋是他们在以色列人中的产业。
verses.en: Whatever someone among the Levites might redeem—the sale of a house which is his property in a city—must revert in the Jubilee,[NOTE:1] because the houses of the cities of the Levites are their property in the midst of the Israelites.
notes: Heb “And which he shall redeem from the Levites shall go out, sale of house and city, his property in the Jubilee.” Although the end of this verse is clear, the first part is notoriously difficult. There are five main views. (1) The first clause of the verse actually attaches to the previous verse, and refers to the fact that their houses retain a perpetual right of redemption (v. 32b), “which any of the Levites may exercise” (v. 33a; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 418, 421). (2) It refers to property that one Levite sells to another Levite, which is then redeemed by still another Levite (v. 33a). In such cases, the property reverts to the original Levite owner in the Jubilee Year (v. 33b; G. J. Wenham, Leviticus [NICOT], 321). (3) It refers to houses in a city that had come to be declared as a Levitical city but had original non-Levitical owners. Once the city was declared to belong to the Levites, however, an owner could only sell his house to a Levite, and he could only redeem it back from a Levite up until the time of the first Jubilee after the city was declared to be a Levitical city. In this case the first part of the verse would be translated, “Such property as may be redeemed from the Levites” (NRSV, NJPS). At the first Jubilee, however, all such houses became the property of the Levites (v. 33b; P. J. Budd, Leviticus [NCBC], 353). (4) It refers to property “which is appropriated from the Levites” (not “redeemed from the Levites,” v. 33a) by those who have bought it or taken it as security for debts owed to them by Levites who had fallen on bad times. Again, such property reverts back to the original Levite owners at the Jubilee (B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 177). (5) It simply refers to the fact that a Levite has the option of redeeming his house (i.e., the prefix form of the verb is taken to be subjunctive, “may or might redeem”), which he had to sell because he had fallen into debt or perhaps even become destitute. Even if he never gained the resources to do so, however, it would still revert to him in the Jubilee year. The present translation is intended to reflect this latter view.

verses.zh: 只是他们各城郊野之地不可卖，因为是他们永远的产业。」
verses.en: Moreover,[NOTE:1] the open field areas of their cities[NOTE:2] must not be sold, because that is their perpetual possession.
notes: Heb “And.”
This refers to the region of fields just outside and surrounding the city where cattle were kept and garden crops were grown (B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 177).

verses.zh: 「你的弟兄在你那里若渐渐贫穷，手中缺乏，你就要帮补他，使他与你同住，像外人和寄居的一样。
verses.en: “‘If your brother[NOTE:1] becomes impoverished and is indebted to you,[NOTE:2] you must support[NOTE:3] him; he must live[NOTE:4] with you like a foreign resident.[NOTE:5]
notes: It is not clear to whom this refers. It is probably broader than “sibling” (cf. NRSV “any of your kin”; NLT “any of your Israelite relatives”) but some English versions take it to mean “fellow Israelite” (so NIV11, TEV; cf. NIV84, NAB “countrymen”) and others are ambiguous (cf. CEV “any of your people”).
Heb “and his hand slips with you.”
Heb “strengthen”; NASB “sustain.”

The form וָחַי (vakhay, “and shall live”) looks like the adjective “living,” but the MT form is simply the same verb written as a double ayin verb (see HALOT 309 s.v. חיה qal, and GKC 218 §76.i; cf. Lev 18:5).

Heb “a foreigner and resident,” which is probably to be combined (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 170-71). The Hebrew terms ger (גֵּר; “resident foreigner”) and toshav (תּוֹשָׁב; “resident/dweller”) have similar meaning. The toshav was less integrated into Israelite society, had less rights, and had not fully committed to the religion of Israel. Here the combination emphasizes the impoverished Israelites change in status. Note that the native born citizen and the resident foreigner (or naturalized citizen) were equal under the law (Exod 12:49; Lev 24:22; Num 9:14; 15:15, 16, 26, 29; 19:10; 35:15; Deut 1:16) or similar obligations (Exod 20:10; 23:12; Lev 16:29; 17:10, 12, 13; 18:26; 24:16; Num 15:14).

verses.zh: 不可向他取利，也不可向他多要；只要敬畏你的　神，使你的弟兄与你同住。
verses.en: Do not take interest or profit from him,[NOTE:1] but you must fear your God, and your brother must live[NOTE:2] with you.
notes: The meaning of the terms rendered “interest” and “profit” is much debated (see the summaries in P. J. Budd, Leviticus [NCBC], 354-55 and B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 178). Verse 37, however, suggests that the first refers to a percentage of money and the second percentage of produce (see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 421).
In form the Hebrew term וְחֵי (vekhey, “shall live”) is the construct plural noun (i.e., “the life of”), but here it is used as the finite verb (cf. v. 35 and GKC 218 §76.i).

verses.zh: 你借钱给他，不可向他取利；借粮给他，也不可向他多要。
verses.en: You must not lend him your money at interest, and you must not sell him food for profit.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your money” and “your food.” With regard to “interest” and “profit” see the note on v. 36 above.

verses.zh: 我是耶和华―你们的　神，曾领你们从埃及地出来，为要把迦南地赐给你们，要作你们的　神。」
verses.en: I am the Lord your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan—to be your God.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to be to you for a God.”

verses.zh: 「你的弟兄若在你那里渐渐穷乏，将自己卖给你，不可叫他像奴仆服事你。
verses.en: “‘If your brother becomes impoverished with regard to you so that he sells himself to you, you must not subject him to slave service.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you shall not serve against him service of a slave.” A distinction is being made here between the status of slave and indentured servant.

verses.zh: 他要在你那里像雇工人和寄居的一样，要服事你直到禧年。
verses.en: He must be with you as a hired worker, as a resident foreigner;[NOTE:1] he must serve with you until the Year of Jubilee,
notes: See the note on Lev 25:6 above.

verses.zh: 到了禧年，他和他儿女要离开你，一同出去归回本家，到他祖宗的地业那里去。
verses.en: but then[NOTE:1] he may go free,[NOTE:2] he and his children with him, and may return to his family and to the property of his ancestors.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have adversative force here.
Heb “may go out from you.”
Heb “fathers.”

verses.zh: 因为他们是我的仆人，是我从埃及地领出来的，不可卖为奴仆。
verses.en: Since the Israelites[NOTE:1] are my servants whom I brought out from the land of Egypt, they must not be sold in a slave sale.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or perhaps reflexive Niphal rather than passive, “they shall not sell themselves [as in] a slave sale.”

verses.zh: 不可严严地辖管他，只要敬畏你的　神。
verses.en: You must not rule over them harshly,[NOTE:1] but you must fear your God.
notes: Heb “You shall not rule in him in violence”; cf. NASB “with severity”; NIV “ruthlessly.”

verses.zh: 至于你的奴仆、婢女，可以从你四围的国中买。
verses.en: “‘As for your male and female slaves[NOTE:1] who may belong to you—you may buy male and female slaves from the nations all around you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And your male slave and your female slave.” Smr has these as plural terms, “slaves,” not singular.
Heb “ from the nations which surround you, from them you shall buy male slave and female slave.”

verses.zh: 并且那寄居在你们中间的外人和他们的家属，在你们地上所生的，你们也可以从其中买人；他们要作你们的产业。
verses.en: Also, you may buy slaves[NOTE:1] from the children of the foreigners who reside with you and from their families that are[NOTE:2] with you, whom they have fathered in your land; they may become your property.
notes: The word “slaves” is not in the Hebrew text, but is implied here.
Heb “family which is” (i.e., singular rather than plural).

verses.zh: 你们要将他们遗留给你们的子孙为产业，要永远从他们中间拣出奴仆；只是你们的弟兄以色列人，你们不可严严地辖管。
verses.en: You may give them as an inheritance to your children after you to possess as property. You may enslave them perpetually. However, as for your brothers the Israelites, no man may rule over his brother harshly.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and your brothers, the sons of Israel, a man in his brother you shall not rule in him in violence.”

verses.zh: 「住在你那里的外人，或是寄居的，若渐渐富足，你的弟兄却渐渐穷乏，将自己卖给那外人，或是寄居的，或是外人的宗族，
verses.en: “‘If a resident foreigner who is with you prospers[NOTE:1] and your brother becomes impoverished with regard to him so that[NOTE:2] he sells himself to a resident foreigner who is with you or to a member[NOTE:3] of a foreigner’s family,
notes: Heb “And if the hand of a foreigner and resident with you reaches” (cf. v. 26 for this idiom).
Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.
Heb “offshoot, descendant.”

verses.zh: 卖了以后，可以将他赎回。无论是他的弟兄，
verses.en: after he has sold himself he retains a right of redemption.[NOTE:1] One of his brothers may redeem him,
notes: Heb “right of redemption shall be to him.”

verses.zh: 或伯叔、伯叔的儿子，本家的近支，都可以赎他。他自己若渐渐富足，也可以自赎。
verses.en: or his uncle or his cousin[NOTE:1] may redeem him, or any one of the rest of his blood relatives—his family[NOTE:2]—may redeem him, or if[NOTE:3] he prospers, he may redeem himself.
notes: Heb “the son of his uncle.”
Heb “or from the remainder of his flesh from his family.”
The LXX, followed by the Syriac, actually has “if,” which is not in the MT.

verses.zh: 他要和买主计算，从卖自己的那年起，算到禧年；所卖的价值照着年数多少，好像工人每年的工价。
verses.en: He must calculate with the one who bought him the number of years[NOTE:1] from the year he sold himself to him until the Jubilee year, and the cost of his sale must correspond to the number of years, according to the rate of wages a hired worker would have earned while with him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the years.”
Heb “as days of a hired worker he shall be with him.” For this and the following verses see the explanation in P. J. Budd, Leviticus (NCBC), 358-59.

verses.zh: 若缺少的年数多，就要按着年数从买价中偿还他的赎价。
verses.en: If there are still many years, in keeping with them,[NOTE:1] he must refund most of the cost of his purchase for his redemption,
notes: Heb “to the mouth of them.”

verses.zh: 若到禧年只缺少几年，就要按着年数和买主计算，偿还他的赎价。
verses.en: but if only a few years remain[NOTE:1] until the Jubilee, he must calculate for himself in keeping with the remaining years and refund it for his redemption.
notes: Heb “but if a little remains in the years.”

verses.zh: 他和买主同住，要像每年雇的工人，买主不可严严地辖管他。
verses.en: He must be with the one who bought him[NOTE:1] like a yearly hired worker.[NOTE:2] The one who bought him[NOTE:3] must not rule over him harshly in your sight.
notes: Heb “be with him”; the referent (the one who bought him) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “As a hired worker year in year.”
Heb “He”; the referent (the one who bought him) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他若不这样被赎，到了禧年，要和他的儿女一同出去。
verses.en: If, however,[NOTE:1] he is not redeemed in these ways, he must go free[NOTE:2] in the Jubilee year, he and his children with him,
notes: Heb “And if.”
Heb “go out.”

verses.zh: 因为以色列人都是我的仆人，是我从埃及地领出来的。我是耶和华―你们的　神。」
verses.en: because the Israelites are my own servants;[NOTE:1] they are my servants whom I brought out from the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
notes: Heb “because to me the sons of Israel are servants.”
